name: Verna
tagline: Small republic, home of the University
summary: A small, neutral republic beside Vesper that survives on treaties instead of an army, and is famous above all for the University of Verna, which Vernans will remind you is theirs and not the other way round.
government: A small independent republic that runs on committees, legal agreements and published minutes, and keeps its neutrality through treaties and guarantees from stronger neighbours.
knownFor: The University of Verna, Gate studies, medicine, precision instruments and printing, neutrality, and saying "we do not know" without embarrassment.
gateAttitude: Study before use: record where everything came from, publish what is true, and restrict the instructions for anything dangerous.
beliefs:
Most Vernans belong to the **Faith of the First Light**, much as their Vesperian neighbours do, and small communities descended from the religious traditions of the Old Scholastic Coast survive alongside them. In keeping with its neutrality, the Republic favours no faith.

What works most like a shared conviction in Verna is the lesson of the Silencing: **knowledge can disappear**. Libraries burn, texts are seized, schools scatter. So the University copies its important materials, catalogues them in more than one collection, keeps them in separate buildings and shares them with trusted institutions. Archivists say *no library should be allowed to die only once*, and a curator who wants to borrow a unique manuscript will be told it can travel as soon as the copy is finished, because until there are two of it, there is only one of it.

Scholars care intensely about **provenance**, and ask *"Where did this come from?"* before *"What does it do?"* They separate what was observed from how it's interpreted, and say which is which. The University takes funding, but not funding that comes with a say over its conclusions, archives or readers: the last time a state decided which books could be read, Verna received the refugees. Restricted research is the big point of friction, and the Vernan line is precise about it: *"We are not restricting the truth. We are restricting the instructions."*
history:
Verna was a republic before it was famous: small, stable, literate and commercially active, with modest colleges of its own. When exactly it was founded, and what those colleges were called, isn't recorded in the Archive's sources.

What changed it was the **Silencing of the Schools**. An older Kharadi empire, the **Qadiri Ascendancy** (not the modern Compact), conquered the **Old Scholastic Coast**, a string of cities famous for philosophy, mathematics, medicine and astronomy, and set out to impose religious and intellectual conformity: schools closed, temples converted, archives seized, books burned, teachers made to renounce forbidden doctrines. One preserved closure order ends *"There is one truth, and it does not require debate"*, and Vernan teachers make their students copy that line out. Many scholars fled to Verna with whatever they could carry, including one copyist who cut the most important pages out of their bindings and sewed them into her family's coats: *"Take the pages. Leave the bindings."* The names of most of the Coast's cities, and how long the Silencing lasted, are among the things it damaged.

The refugees didn't bring learning to Verna. They found it there and made it much larger, until the colleges grew into the modern **University**. Vernans are particular about this: it's a Vernan institution transformed by exile, not a Coast school that moved house. The Ascendancy is gone now. The Coast passed to the **Mirzal Regency**, whose cities never reopened their great schools, and which is in a crisis the Archive can't yet describe. Some Kharadi institutions still hold manuscripts and instruments taken from the Coast, and whether they should come back is an argument that keeps surfacing in diplomacy and auction houses.

Verna keeps no large army. Its security is a web of treaties: it stays neutral, foreign powers don't station troops there without broad agreement, and its neighbours guarantee its borders, because Verna is useful to all of them: neutral ground, a host of conferences, a source of doctors and instruments, a keeper of archives. As one Vernan diplomat put it: *"We do not need everyone to love us. We need everyone to prefer us unconquered."* Vernans like to say that Vesper argues in the street and Verna argues in committee, and publishes the minutes.

**The Gates.** Verna's reach in Endros comes through the University: its laboratories, its archaeologists, the Expeditioners it sponsors and its close work with the Gate Evaluation Committee, which it founded and which is now a separate body (see Endros and the Gates). Its approach is *study before use*: record where everything came from, publish what is true, and restrict the instructions for anything dangerous. Vesperian colleagues argue about that constantly. *"Knowledge belongs to everyone."* *"So does the explosion."*
visualSummary:
Verna is temperate, hilly and densely lived-in: orchards, vineyards, hill towns, stone bridges and old roads, with observatories and library towers among them. Nothing feels like wilderness. Buildings are warm pale stone with slate roofs, courtyards, colonnades and botanical gardens, meant to be worked in for centuries rather than to impress an ambassador (though they usually manage both). Deep green is the colour of Verna, on banners, robes and the flag, and the favourite motif is the **compass rose**, with stars, books and natural forms.

Clothing is refined and practical: long coats, fitted vests, neck scarves, spectacles, satchels and instrument cases. Scholars wear academic robes in their faculty's colours, and students read each other's scarf trim and start arguing on the steps. Ordinary Vernans don't dress like professors, because most of them aren't. The economy runs on precision rather than heavy industry: lenses, surgical tools, astronomical instruments and printing. A good Vernan instrument-maker writes down how wrong an instrument might be, because a buyer can trust that and should never trust one that claims to be perfect.

The Vernan manner is composed, careful and politely sceptical, and the most Vernan sentence is *"The evidence does not currently support that conclusion."* The big foreign stereotype is that every Vernan works at the University. Vernans find it endlessly irritating. The country has farms, printing houses, hospitals and town councils, and a pear farmer who has been asked which faculty he teaches in will tell you no, he doesn't teach philosophy, though the University does buy a remarkable number of pears.
palette: Deep green, ivory, gold and slate blue, with burgundy accents
materials: Pale stone, slate, brass instruments, paper and good cloth

relations.text: Its larger neighbour: shared academic culture, constant argument over restricted research.
Cooperative but guarded: welcomes imperial funding, resists imperial priorities.
Study it first versus test it: different methods, mutual benefit.
Mutual scholarly respect built on archives and long memory; access to Tianzhao's records stays limited.
Trades with it, but stays especially wary of depending on Kharadi credit or patronage.

sponsorFraming: The Recruitment Faction is the **University of Verna**, which sponsors scholars and specialists from anywhere: being sponsored by the University is not the same as being Vernan.
extraRule: Once between expeditions, when you make a Research Project Action, gain +1 additional Progress if the University's laboratories, archives, specialists or equipment could reasonably assist you.
